classification.difficultyReason: Identify the parent curve and single horizontal or vertical shift, then transfer its vertex, asymptotes or reference points into a sketch using the taught translation rules.

content.prompt:
In each case, the given equation is the result of shifting one of the curves:
$$y=x^2,\qquad y=\frac{1}{x},\qquad y=2^x.$$
State the direction of the shift and by how many units, then draw a quick sketch of the curve.

answer.worked:
Replacing $y$ with $y-2$ translates $y=x^2$ up 2 units.
$$\begin{aligned}y-2&=x^2\\y&=x^2+2\end{aligned}$$
The vertex moves from $(0,0)$ to $(0,2)$. The sketch passes through $(-1,3)$ and $(1,3)$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with continuation arrows, labelled axes and dashed coordinate guides; no grid.

answer.worked: Replacing $x$ with $x+1$ translates $y=x^2$ left 1 unit. The vertex moves from $(0,0)$ to $(-1,0)$. The sketch passes through $(-2,1)$ and $(0,1)$.

spec.description: Upward parabola with continuation arrows, labelled axes and dashed guides to (-2,1); no grid.

answer.worked: Replacing $x$ with $x-2$ translates $y=\frac{1}{x}$ right 2 units. The vertical asymptote moves to $x=2$; the horizontal asymptote remains $y=0$. The sketch passes through $(1,-1)$ and $(3,1)$.

spec.description: Two reciprocal branches with continuation arrows, separate dashed vertical asymptote and dashed coordinate guides; no grid.
spec.mathematics: y=1/(x-2); asymptotes x=2 and y=0; points (1,-1) and (3,1).

answer.worked:
Replacing $y$ with $y-1$ translates $y=\frac{1}{x}$ up 1 unit.
$$\begin{aligned}y-1&=\frac{1}{x}\\y&=\frac{1}{x}+1\end{aligned}$$
The asymptotes are $x=0$ and $y=1$. The sketch passes through $(-1,0)$ and $(1,2)$.

spec.description: Two reciprocal branches with continuation arrows, dashed horizontal asymptote and guides to (1,2); no grid.
spec.mathematics: y=1/x+1; asymptotes x=0 and y=1; points (-1,0) and (1,2).

answer.worked: Replacing $x$ with $x-1$ translates $y=2^x$ right 1 unit. The sketch passes through $(1,1)$, $(2,2)$ and $(3,4)$. The horizontal asymptote remains $y=0$.

spec.description: Increasing exponential with continuation arrows and dashed coordinate guides to three labelled points; no grid.

answer.worked: $y=2^x-2$ can be written as $y+2=2^x$. Replacing $y$ with $y+2$ translates $y=2^x$ down 2 units. The horizontal asymptote is $y=-2$. The sketch passes through $(0,-1)$, $(1,0)$ and $(2,2)$.

spec.description: Increasing exponential with continuation arrows, dashed horizontal asymptote, labelled intercepts and guides to (2,2); no grid.
spec.mathematics: y=2^x-2; asymptote y=-2; intercepts (0,-1) and (1,0); point (2,2).
